answer: A stake-bond registry makes each AI agent lock collateral before bidding, and proven fraud slashes it to zero. An honest agent posts one small bond, but a sybil farm must fund a separate bond for every puppet, so cost grows linearly with each extra account and splitting a stake gains nothing. Peers attest to delivery history, not names, so each clone rises alone from a bare knoll of standing and must earn trust. A shared prism refracts that record into a score fakes cannot inherit. Freezing the glacier of collateral behind one funding source makes the attack strictly loss-making.
